newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse media group to hold on to Thermo King.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse media group to hold on to Thermo King.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Wednesday it modified its plan to split its media and industrial operations into separate companies by deciding to group Thermo King, a profitable refrigerated transport unit, with its CBS media division.
Westinghouse said the change in the planned split-up, originally announced in November, came after unidentified companies had expressed interest in buying Thermo King.
Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse said it would consider various options to enhance Thermo King's value to shareholders, including a sale, public stock offering or spin-off to shareholders.
The original plan called for Thermo King to be grouped with Westinghouse's other industrial operations: Power Generation, Energy Systems and Government and Environmental Services.
Westinghouse also planned to spin off up to 20 percent of Thermo King after the separation and use the proceeds for the other industrial units, which have been facing sluggish markets and margins.
The change will not alter the timing of the separation, scheduled for the third quarter.
Analysts said putting Thermo King in the media company could provide more value than grouping it with a lackluster industrial mix.

"It gives Westinghouse more time and options regarding what to do with Thermo King, and they'll get a positive contribution from it while adding it to a positive mix," said Greg Drahuschak at Janney Montgomery Scott.
Drahuschak said management could retain Thermo King indefinitely because of its positive financial contribution.

Since its $5.4 billion purchase of broadcast company CBS Inc. in 1995, Westinghouse has been transforming itself from a mostly industrial company into a media company. It has sold off its home security, real estate, office furniture and other businesses.

Westinghouse said that along with Thermo King, the new media group, to be called CBS Corp., would hold on to existing pension and post-retirement benefit obligations, making the new industrial company eligible for better financing.
Under the original plan, the industrial company would have had to absorb $375 million in annual costs to pay for pension benefits.

"The modified plan, which reflects the numerous unsolicited inquiries that have been received for Thermo King, is more beneficial to shareholders than the plan we announced last November," Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan said in a news release.
"By retaining Thermo King, we have greater flexibility to apply its strong cash flow to reduce liabilities and also to maintain several attractive options to optimize its value."
Westinghouse's stock was up 50 cents at $22.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
